t: Of the amount made available under this head in the Department of Agriculture and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1967, for “Payments to States and Puerto Rico”, $166,000 shall be transferred to the subappropriation for “Retirement and employees’ compensation costs for extension agents”.

fable.w: This section only transfers appropriated funds from one account to another. The tempting reading is that the reference to "Payments to States and Puerto Rico" signals involvement of states, but that is only the name of an appropriation heading. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision.
fable.s: $166,000 shall be transferred to the subappropriation for “Retirement and employees’ compensation costs for extension agents”

qwen_block.w: This section describes an internal transfer of funds between two subappropriations within a federal agency's budget. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or decision-making input from any party outside the federal government. The mention of 'States and Puerto Rico' refers to the name of a funding category, not to a participatory process involving those entities.
qwen_block.s: Of the amount made available under this head in the Department of Agriculture and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1967, for “Payments to States and Puerto Rico”, $166,000 shall be transferred to the subappropriation for “Retirement and employees’ compensation costs for extension agents”.

opus.w: This section only moves money from one appropriation account to another. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The mention of "States and Puerto Rico" is just the name of an account, so no one outside the federal government is involved in a federal decision.
opus.s: $166,000 shall be transferred to the subappropriation for “Retirement and employees’ compensation costs for extension agents”.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely administrative and budgetary provision that directs the transfer of funds between specific appropriations accounts. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by non-federal entities in the decision-making process. The mention of 'extension agents' refers to the recipients of the compensation costs, not to a participatory body influencing a federal decision.
qwen_chat.s: Of the amount made available under this head in the Department of Agriculture and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1967, for “Payments to States and Puerto Rico”, $166,000 shall be transferred to the subappropriation for “Retirement and employees’ compensation costs for extension agents”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that transferring funds to "extension agents" implies some form of consultation or coordination with state or local entities, as extension services often involve state universities. However, the text itself is purely a budgetary directive regarding the reallocation of appropriated funds within the federal budget structure. It does not mandate any interaction, consultation, or coordination with outside parties; it simply moves money from one line item to another.
